\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قضاوت} \fa{کردن} (qezâvat kardan)}{قضاوت کردن (qezâvat kardan)}]{\fa{قضاوت} \fa{کردن} (qezâvat kardan) — to judge}

\label{lesson:FA-C365-qezavat-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a rumour, then the Persian for to deny.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قضاوت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{قضاوت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{qezâvat kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to judge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{زود} \fa{درباره} \fa{دیگران} \fa{قضاوت} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u zud darbâre-ye digarân qezâvat mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She is quick to judge other people.
\end{quote}

\emph{Qezâvat} \textquotedblleft{}judgement\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan} (stem \emph{kon-}). \emph{Darbâre-ye kasi qezâvat kardan} — to judge someone. It also means to referee a match.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{قضاوت}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{qaḍāwa} \textquotedblleft{}judging\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from the same Arabic family as \emph{qāḍī} \textquotedblleft{}a judge\textquotedblright{}; \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qezâvat kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qezâvat kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{qezâvat kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a rumour, then the Persian for to deny, then say \emph{qezâvat kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{قضاوت} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To judge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{انتقاد} (enteqâd)}{انتقاد (enteqâd)}]{\fa{انتقاد} (enteqâd) — criticism}

\label{lesson:FA-C365-enteqad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to deny, then the Persian for to judge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{انتقاد}}
\textbf{\fa{انتقاد}} (\emph{enteqâd}) — \textquotedblleft{}criticism\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{به} \fa{انتقاد} \fa{گوش} \fa{میدهد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u be enteqâd gush midahad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He listens to criticism.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{enteqâdât} or \emph{enteqâdhâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{انتقاد}} comes from Arabic \emph{intiqād} \textquotedblleft{}criticism\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{انتقاد} \fa{کردن} (enteqâd kardan)}{انتقاد کردن (enteqâd kardan)}]{\fa{انتقاد} \fa{کردن} (enteqâd kardan) — to criticise}

\label{lesson:FA-C365-enteqad-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to judge, then the Persian for criticism.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{انتقاد} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{انتقاد} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{enteqâd kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to criticise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مردم} \fa{از} \fa{دولت} \fa{انتقاد} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mardom az dowlat enteqâd kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People criticised the government.
\end{quote}

Takes \emph{az}: \emph{az kasi enteqâd kardan}. Stem \emph{kon-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{انتقاد} \fa{کردن}} joins \emph{enteqâd}, from Arabic \emph{intiqād} \textquotedblleft{}criticism\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), to the inherited Persian verb \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اغراق} \fa{کردن} (eghrâq kardan)}{اغراق کردن (eghrâq kardan)}]{\fa{اغراق} \fa{کردن} (eghrâq kardan) — to exaggerate}

\label{lesson:FA-C365-eghraq-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for criticism, then the Persian for to criticise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اغراق} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{اغراق} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{eghrâq kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to exaggerate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{همیشه} \fa{اغراق} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u hamishe eghrâq mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He exaggerates all the time.
\end{quote}

\emph{Eghrâq} \textquotedblleft{}exaggeration\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan}. \emph{Dar chizi eghrâq kardan} — to exaggerate something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اغراق}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ighrāq} \textquotedblleft{}exaggeration\textquotedblright{}; \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is the inherited Persian verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{توجیه} \fa{کردن} (towjih kardan)}{توجیه کردن (towjih kardan)}]{\fa{توجیه} \fa{کردن} (towjih kardan) — to justify}

\label{lesson:FA-C365-towjih-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to criticise, then the Persian for to exaggerate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{توجیه} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{توجیه} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{towjih kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to justify\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{نمیتواند} \fa{رفتارش} \fa{را} \fa{توجیه} \fa{کند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u nemitavânad raftârash râ towjih konad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He cannot justify his behaviour.
\end{quote}

\emph{Towjih} \textquotedblleft{}justification; explanation\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan}. It also means to brief someone on a task.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{توجیه}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{tawjīh} (EtymDB), a verbal noun usually explained as turning something to face the right way; \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
